text:
nina: Hey all - first day. VPN (Okta AnyConnect split-tunnel) seems to connect, but my Mac (Ventura) can't reach internal artifactory at artifactory.internal.redwood.dev:443. Browser times out, curl hangs. Any Mac-specific gotchas?
ashok: welcome! two things to check: (1) Are you behind a company proxy (HTTP_PROXY) set in your env? (2) Does `scutil --dns` on Mac show the VPN DNS server for the 10.40. domain?
nina: scutil shows DNS for the VPN interface but Curl still goes to public IP. I noticed we have a corporate HTTP proxy configured in System Settings for some networks. Could that override split-tunnel routing?
matt: yeah proxies can reroute HTTP(S) traffic. For artifactory we should go direct over the VPN. Try `curl --noproxy "*.internal.redwood.dev" -v https://artifactory.internal.redwood.dev/` and see if that reaches it.
nina: tried that and it works — `--noproxy` succeeds. So the system proxy was intercepting.
ashok: for a permanent fix, either add an exclusion for `*.internal.redwood.dev` in your Mac proxy settings or set `no_proxy`/`NO_PROXY` env var in your shell and GUI apps (some apps ignore env). If you want infra to push a global exception for managed machines, open a ticket.
infra-bot: Docs: https://wiki.redwood.internal/vpn/macos-proxy-note. If you need help opening a ticket use the infra template.
nina: great, adding `NO_PROXY=*.internal.redwood.dev` to my ~/.zprofile for now. Thanks everyone! I'll post a short note in #onboarding about the proxy gotcha.
